note: R8: "The exact number of deaths from the atomic bombing is still unknown. Estimates place the number of dead by the end of December 1945 ... at roughly 140,000." Quoted as the city's.

title: Nagasaki Peace site: the atomic bombing (City of Nagasaki)
author: City of Nagasaki
note: R8: by the end of December 1945, 73,884 killed and 74,909 injured (the July 1950 report of the Committee for the Preservation of Atomic Bomb Artifacts).

title: The Effects of Atomic Bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki
author: USSBS Chairman's Office
note: Its figures (70,000–80,000 at Hiroshima; 35,000–40,000 at Nagasaki) known here through R8, which marks the source opened for the figures; the text itself not reopened in this pass.

title: 沖縄県平和祈念資料館 設立理念 (founding statement, 1975, revised 2000)
author: Okinawa Prefectural Peace Memorial Museum
note: Read by R8 through the prefecture's PDF: civilian deaths 「10数万」, more than soldiers; some 「自ら命を断たされ」, some 「敗走する自国軍隊の犠牲にされる」.

title: The Cornerstone of Peace (平和の礎)
author: Okinawa Prefecture
note: R8: every name of the dead of the Battle of Okinawa, "regardless of their nationality or military or civilian status"; 242,225 names in June 2024.

title: Power of Words Handbook (2013, revised 2020)
author: Japanese American Citizens League
note: R8: "incarceration", not "internment"; "some 110,000 ... (of which nearly 70% were American citizens)".

author: United States Congress

author: Australian War Memorial
